questions.question: A motorcyclist should constantly look ahead at the road for:
questions.explanation: Look ahead to notice changes in traffic and road conditions, and to identify escape routes. Be ready to react quickly to any changes.

questions.question: When should a rider check their mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down or stopping, at intersections, when changing lanes, and when turning.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Not wear a jacket if it's warm out.
Always wear a jacket, even if it's warm out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket, even if it's warm out.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket to protect yourself, even in warm weather. A jacket helps prevent injury and dehydration. Also wear long pants and tuck in shoelaces so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: You should fully check your motorcycle:
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more attention than cars. Check your entire motorcycle before each ride.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, motorcycle riders should especially watch for:

options.text: Drivers looking for a parking spot.
Cars pulling out of parking spaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars pulling out of parking spaces.
questions.explanation: When passing parked vehicles, be alert. A car may suddenly pull away from the curb or leave a parking space.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road hazards or conditions.

questions.question: A plastic face shield protects riders from:
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your face from injury in a crash and shields you from wind, dust, dirt, rain, insects, and rocks kicked up by other vehicles.

questions.question: Because alcohol does not need to be digested, it means that:

options.text: Alcohol reaches the brain and affects the drinker within minutes.
The alcohol never leaves the body.
It takes a long time to feel the effects of alcohol.
Your body removes alcohol very quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol reaches the brain and affects the drinker within minutes.
questions.explanation: Alcohol enters the bloodstream quickly without needing digestion. It reaches the brain within minutes. Your body removes alcohol slowly—about one drink per hour.

questions.question: Slippery surfaces make motorcycles hard to control. Which of these is a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted road markings, and metal covers are slippery surfaces. Ride with extra care on these surfaces.

questions.question: When carrying a load on your motorcycle, place it:

options.text: On only one side of the bike.
In a way that requires you to hold it.

questions.explanation: Place loads forward, over or in front of the rear axle. Loads placed behind the rear axle can make turning and braking difficult and may cause the motorcycle to wobble.

questions.question: Most crashes happen in daylight. How can you be more visible?
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen in daylight. Always wear bright-colored clothing while riding, even during the day.

questions.question: How can you increase your visibility?

options.text: Add extra lights to your motorcycle.
Do not use your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Add extra lights to your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: You can increase visibility by wearing bright or reflective clothing, adding extra lights to your motorcycle, using turn signals, and flashing your brake light when needed.

questions.question: When riding, what should you do?

options.text: Always look ahead and watch for potential dangers.
Focus on the controls and speedometer instead of the road.
Do not worry about hazards—they are rare on the road.
Look ahead but do not look for hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always look ahead and watch for potential dangers.
questions.explanation: Always look well ahead of your motorcycle to spot hazards early. This helps you react before you reach them.

questions.question: Before every ride, check all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your rims and spokes for damage, tire condition and tread, and all lights. You do not need to check the seat fabric.

questions.question: A driver is tailgating you. What should you do?

options.text: Move to one side of your lane to let them share it.

questions.explanation: The best way to handle tailgating is to let the other driver pass. Change lanes safely and let them go ahead. Speeding up will only make the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: A used helmet with visible cracks:

options.text: May not work properly and should not be used.
Is okay if it still fits snugly.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not work properly and should not be used.
questions.explanation: Helmets must meet DOT standards and have no damage. A cracked helmet should be replaced.

questions.question: Riding with a passenger:

options.text: Does not change how the motorcycle handles.
Is usually safe for new riders.
Is good practice for new riders.

questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle, which changes how it handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: On which surface does a motorcycle have the best grip?
questions.explanation: Dry pavement provides the best grip. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, and metal plates all reduce traction.

questions.question: If your motorcycle chain or belt breaks, what happens?

options.text: The rear wheel gets more power.
The front wheel gets more power.

questions.explanation: If your chain or belt breaks, your rear wheel will suddenly lose power.

questions.question: A face shield:

options.text: Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic face shield provides the best protection for your eyes and face. Eyeglasses are not a good substitute.
